newsitem.title: GERMANY: German M3 growth outpacing Buba's plans -- Welteke.
newsitem.headline: German M3 growth outpacing Buba's plans -- Welteke.

text.p: German M3 money supply was growing more quickly than the Bundesbank envisioned, but markets had not interpreted as a revival of price pressures, a senior central bank official said on Monday.

"M3 is clearly growing more strongly than the Bundesbank had planned, but this has not been interpreted by the markets as an indication that this will create inflationary pressures," Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke told foreign journalists.

In January, M3 grew at an annualised, seasonally adjusted rate of 11.7 percent, compared with the fourth quarter average rate of 1996, outpacing the central bank's self-imposed growth corridor of 3-1/2 to 6-1/2 percent.
Welteke, also president of the state central bank in Hesse, said weak monetary capital formation was a key reason for high M3 growth rates.

Saying it was little wonder investors were not parking their money in longer-dated securities, considering the current low capital market rates, he said investors were evidently parking money in short-term funds.
M3 money supply is comprised of cash in circulation, time, sight and short-term savings deposits.
